_note: Saved Gemini diagnosis responses for the 3 demo photos, plus a default for other uploads in DEMO_MODE.

actions: Keep watering only when the top 2 inches of soil are dry
Deadhead nothing: the flowers turn into berries birds love
Check again in about two weeks

candidates.label: Fungal leaf spot
candidates.evidence: Round brown spots with yellow halos on several lower leaves, typical after warm, wet weeks.

candidates.label: Spider mites
candidates.evidence: A little stippling near the leaf edges, but no webbing is visible.

candidates.label: Cold damage
candidates.evidence: Some leaf margins are darker, though the pattern is spotty rather than edge-wide.

actions: Pick off the spotted leaves and put them in the trash, not the compost
Water at the base in the morning so leaves dry quickly
Give the plant more air by trimming any stems touching its neighbors
Take another photo in one week to see if new leaves stay clean
This looks like Mexican petunia, which is invasive in Florida
Dig out the plant and its runners before it sets seed, and bag it
Replace it with native wild petunia for the same purple flowers

candidates.label: Possible leaf spot
candidates.evidence: A few small dark spots, but the photo is too far away to be sure.

actions: Take a closer, well-lit photo of one affected leaf
Remove fallen leaves from under the plant
Avoid wetting the leaves when you water
